recognitions.title: This week, three separate claims of having fixed something didn't survive a single news cycle
recognitions.explanation: Across trade, foreign policy and debt management, the same pattern showed up: an announcement of control or resolution, followed within about a day by the other side, or the market, contradicting it. This week one of the three went all the way - the Canada 'deal' didn't just fail to hold, it collapsed entirely into real tariffs and real retaliation. A denial that talks with Iran even exist, followed a day later by a declared war footing against that same government. A bond-market intervention whose relief lasted less than 24 hours before yields fully round-tripped. The pattern isn't that these claims are false when made - it's that none of them are built to survive contact with the next news cycle.

evidence.text: Canada's retaliatory tariffs took effect as threatened at 12:01am Sept 8 - and instead of settling into a new equilibrium, Trump answered within two days by banning Canadian dairy, alcohol and motorcycles outright. A "resolution" by tariff rate lasted less than 48 hours before the tool itself changed.

Two days after CENTCOM denied Iran's destroyer-strike claim, Iran fired roughly 20 ballistic missiles at US and Jordanian bases overnight - the strait war's most kinetic night yet. Whatever "de-escalation" the denial implied didn't survive the news cycle that followed it.

The 10-year has now reversed direction three times in five sessions: a Fed-comment-driven high above 4.81%, a dovish-remark dip to 4.74-4.77%, and a bounce back to 4.79% on a stronger-than-forecast August jobs report, pushing rate-hike odds back up to ~52%. No single reading has held for even a full trading day.

recognitions.title: Three things that looked like resolutions this week all deferred the real question to later
recognitions.explanation: A ceasefire, a court ruling, and a shipping framework all landed this week wearing the shape of a resolution — and in each case, the people closest to it said out loud that the actual question is still open. A peace roadmap got its first verification mission, not a verified peace. A Supreme Court stay resolved a procedural fight while its own justices noted the underlying legality is untouched. A transit deal is 'in principle' and 'still being finalized.' Each is a real step. None of them is the thing a headline would make it sound like.

evidence.text: M23 declared DRC's Ebola outbreak over in its territory in late June; as of Sept 7 the count reached 6,686 confirmed and 3,226 dead, officially making this the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in Congo's history - and it crossed that line while the conflict-surveillance gap that let the resurgence through was still open, not after it closed.

DOJ's own statement went further than the judge's actual ruling, calling NY's Climate Superfund Act "unconstitutional" rather than just preempted - while state Sen. Liz Krueger, the bill's co-sponsor, is publicly telling the AG "we believe that we will win" on appeal. Both sides are already arguing a case bigger than the one the judge decided.

"Just days away" from a done deal is where Iran's Oman safe-passage talks have sat for over a month - the same negotiation track that produced a US strike on a wedding in Kuhestak on Sept 1, four to five dead. A framework repeatedly described as nearly finished still hasn't actually finished.

Kocharyan's own lawyer now says his case will be appealed to the ECHR or a UN body, calling it a mandatory legal step rather than an escalation. A domestic corruption case that looked settled by detention is instead expanding outward, putting Armenia's judiciary itself in front of international scrutiny.
